channel.description: New research across consciousness, quantum foundations, and neuroscience.

item.title: Designing fault-tolerant blind quantum computation
item.description: Blind quantum computing (BQC) allows a client with limited quantum capabilities to delegate quantum computations to a more powerful server while hiding the computation. Existing protocols face significant challenges when scaling to large-scale fault-tolerant computations due to large communication overhead, photon losses, and low efficiencies.

item.title: Qutrit quantum neural network with non-commutative multi-subspace feature map
item.description: We present QNN-3L, a quantum neural network architecture based on three-level systems (qutrits) with longitudinal Ising-type couplings on a one-dimensional lattice. Starting from an explicit phenomenological multilevel Hamiltonian that includes local anharmonicity, diagonal couplings and resonant control pulses, we derive native selective rotations on computational subspaces and a nearest-neighbour controlled-\((Z)\) primitive.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence in Physics Research: Foundations, Applications and Challenges for Autonomous Scientific Discovery
item.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used across physics research, but claims that it now produces autonomous scientific discovery require careful scrutiny. This narrative review aims to synthesize evidence published between January 2014 and August 2026, together with earlier foundational works, on how AI is used in physics and to evaluate the extent to which its contributions amount to validated discovery rather than prediction.

item.title: The functional fallacy: a diagnostic framework for functional claims in the psychology of consciousness
item.description: Scientific theories of consciousness (STOCs) routinely claim, in one form or another, that consciousness does something: that it confers a function and a behavioral or adaptive advantage. This paper asks what that claim can coherently amount to.

item.title: Consciousness, complexity, and clinical implications
item.description: Consciousness remains one of science's most challenging problems because it cannot be exhaustively characterized as a single function, computation, or behavior; it also refers to the presence and organization of subjective experience. This position paper integrates clinical neurology, neurophysiology, psychiatry, psychoanalysis, embodied cognition, moral neuroscience, theoretical physics, philosophy of mind, and neurotechnology.

item.title: Benchmarking and resource analysis for augmented-Lagrangian quantum Hamiltonian descent
item.description: Quantum Hamiltonian Descent (QHD) is a continuous optimization algorithm based on simulating a time-dependent quantum Hamiltonian whose potential energy encodes the objective function and whose kinetic energy promotes exploration through quantum interference and tunneling. While QHD is formulated for unconstrained optimization, many real-world optimization problems are constrained and highly nonconvex.

item.title: Tunable spectral correlations of highly multimode visible light via broadband quantum frequency conversion
item.description: Multimode squeezed states of light are a resource for achieving quantum advantage in computing and sensing, where spatial or temporal modes have been the experimental norm. In our experiments, we generated highly frequency-multimode infrared quantum light and showed how adiabatic frequency conversion can be used to convert the quantum state to visible wavelengths while concurrently manipulating the joint spectrum by realizing a configurable many-port frequency-domain beamsplitter unitary transformation.

item.title: Time Travel Paradoxes and Entangled Timelines
item.description: For time travel to be consistent with the known laws of physics, the resulting paradoxes must be resolved. It has been suggested that the notion of parallel timelines may provide a resolution, by allowing different events to happen in different timelines.

item.title: Quantum recurrent unit: an effective and parameter-efficient quantum neural network architecture for NISQ devices
item.description: The rapid growth of modern machine learning models presents fundamental challenges in parameter efficiency and computational resource requirements. We introduce the Quantum Recurrent Unit (QRU), a novel quantum neural network architecture specifically designed to address these challenges while maintaining compatibility with Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices.

item.title: Logical entangling by qubit permutations in hypergraph products
item.description: Logical entangling gates are a major source of physical spacetime overhead in fault-tolerant quantum computation. Phantom codes reduce this cost by implementing every ordered in-block logical CNOT through physical qubit permutations and Pauli-frame updates.

item.title: Dopamine dynamics in a mouse model of temporal lobe seizures with impaired consciousness
item.description: OBJECTIVE: Focal temporal lobe seizures often lead to impaired consciousness. Recent work has shown depressed cortical arousal, with slow waves and decreased cortical acetylcholine as a possible mechanism for impaired consciousness in focal seizures.
